summary:
Lunar Navigator – Intelligent Lunar Landing Site Analysis

Lunar Navigator is a web-based decision-support platform designed to help mission planners evaluate and compare potential lunar landing sites, particularly around the Moon's South Pole.

The platform brings together lunar landing-site information, Sun and Earth positioning, terrain and horizon profiles, solar illumination, and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication visibility. It provides interactive visualizations, telemetry displays, and a mission trade-off analysis interface to help users understand the environmental and operational conditions at different landing locations and times.

The application includes features such as an interactive lunar globe, 2D polar maps, 3D terrain and shadow visualization, solar power analysis, communication visibility monitoring, and site comparison tools.

For the initial prototype, structured JSON datasets are used to organize landing-site information, ephemeris observations, terrain metadata, horizon profiles, visibility intervals, mission scenarios, and telemetry readings. These datasets provide a foundation for backend integration and future incorporation of scientific data from NASA and JPL sources.

Objective: To provide an interactive and data-driven platform that supports informed lunar landing-site selection and mission planning by bringing important environmental and communication considerations into one interface.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Lunar Navigator is an interactive web platform that helps users explore and compare potential lunar landing sites, particularly near the Moon's South Pole. It visualizes terrain, Sun and Earth positions, solar illumination, power availability, and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication visibility to support mission planning.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Helps compare potential lunar landing sites.
  • Provides insights into sunlight and solar power availability.
  • Evaluates terrain conditions and communication visibility.
  • Supports time-based mission planning and scenario comparisons.
  • Presents complex information through interactive visualizations.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to make lunar landing-site analysis easier, more accessible, and efficient. Lunar Navigator aims to support better-informed mission decisions by bringing important environmental and operational factors into one platform.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript.
  • Backend: Python.
  • Data format: JSON.
  • Development environment: Visual Studio Code.
  • Scientific data sources planned: NASA LOLA, NASA PGDA, and JPL Horizons.
  • Hardware: Standard computer/laptop for development and testing.

5. How is your project creative?

Lunar Navigator combines an interactive lunar globe, 2D polar maps, 3D terrain visualization, 360° horizon analysis, solar power monitoring, and communication visibility into one platform. Its Trade-Off Lab also allows users to experiment with different landing sites and mission timelines.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Our team considered several important factors affecting lunar landing-site suitability:

  • Solar illumination: Availability of sunlight for power generation.
  • Communication visibility: Opportunities for direct communication with Earth.
  • Terrain characteristics: Elevation, slope, surface features, and surrounding horizon.
  • Mission timing: How environmental conditions change with time and launch delays.
  • Site accessibility and suitability: Comparing different lunar locations, particularly near the South Pole.
  • Mission reliability: Understanding potential power and communication limitations.
dataRefs: NASA’s Planetary Geology, Geophysics and Geochemistry Laboratory
